title: CUET General Test Test 2
subject: General Test (Code: 501)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/General Test - 501.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: CUET (UG) 2025 and 2026 General Test shift analyses (no questions copied)

instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Odd one out among perfect squares
questions.question: Choose the number that does not belong with the others: 121, 144, 168, 196
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 168
Answer steps: 121 = 11², 144 = 12², 196 = 14², but 168 is not a perfect square.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all squares of whole numbers.
Key point: Test each number for a common property.

questions.sub_topic: Area of a path around a rectangular park
questions.question: A rectangular park measures 60 m by 40 m. A path 5 m wide runs all around it on the outside. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 1100 m²
Given: park 60 m × 40 m; path 5 m wide outside.
Step 1: Outer rectangle = (60 + 10) × (40 + 10) = 70 × 50 = 3500 m².
Step 2: Path = 3500 − 60 × 40 = 3500 − 2400 = 1100 m².
Common mistake: multiplying the park's perimeter by the width (200 × 5 = 1000 m², option B), which leaves out the four corner squares, or treating the path as inside the park (2400 − 50 × 30 = 900 m², option C).

questions.sub_topic: Direction after two turns
questions.question: Meena is facing east. She turns 90° clockwise and then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) North
Answer steps: from east, 90° clockwise faces south; from south, 180° anticlockwise faces north.
Why not the others: (A) stops after the first turn. (B) turns the first 90° anticlockwise. (D) treats the two turns as cancelling.
Key point: Clockwise: N → E → S → W → N.

questions.sub_topic: National park of the one-horned rhinoceros
questions.question: Kaziranga National Park, home to the largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros, is in which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assam
Why: Kaziranga, on the floodplains of the Brahmaputra in Assam, holds about two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinos. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985) and a tiger reserve.
Why not the others: (A) has Jaldapara, (B) has Dudhwa, both with smaller rhino populations. (D) has Namdapha, known for other species.
Key point: Kaziranga and Manas (both in Assam) are natural World Heritage Sites.

questions.sub_topic: Chronology of four events of the freedom struggle
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order (earliest first):
A. Dandi March
B. Quit India Movement
C. Partition of Bengal
D. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) C, D, A, B
Why: Partition of Bengal (1905), Jallianwala Bagh massacre (April 1919), Dandi March (March–April 1930) and the Quit India Movement (August 1942).
Why not the others: (A) puts the Dandi March before Jallianwala Bagh. (B) puts Jallianwala Bagh before the Partition of Bengal. (D) puts Quit India before the Dandi March.
Key point: 1905, 1919, 1930, 1942.

questions.sub_topic: Papal name of Robert Francis Prevost
questions.question: Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost, elected Pope on 8 May 2025 as the first pope from the United States, took which papal name?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Leo XIV
Why: Prevost, born in Chicago, was elected the 267th pope on the fourth ballot of the conclave on 8 May 2025 and chose the name Leo XIV. He succeeded Pope Francis, who died on 21 April 2025.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not names taken by any pope; the most recent popes were John Paul II, Benedict XVI and Francis.
Key point: Leo XIV is the first pope from the United States and the second from the Americas, after Francis (Argentina).

questions.sub_topic: Relation of a grandson through a daughter
questions.question: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Grandson
Answer steps: B is C's daughter and A is B's brother, so A is C's son. D is C's father, so A is D's grandson (A is male, being a brother).
Why not the others: (B) skips a generation. (C) would need A to be a child of D's sibling. (D) gives the wrong gender for A.
Key point: Work one link at a time and note the gender words.

questions.sub_topic: Place of the Buddha's first sermon
questions.question: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon after attaining enlightenment?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Sarnath
Why: The Buddha gave his first sermon at the Deer Park in Sarnath, near Varanasi. The event is called Dharmachakra Pravartana, "turning the wheel of law".
Why not the others: (A) is where he attained enlightenment. (C) is where he died (mahaparinirvana). (D), in present-day Nepal, is where he was born.
Key point: Lumbini — birth; Bodh Gaya — enlightenment; Sarnath — first sermon; Kushinagar — death.

questions.sub_topic: Gas known as laughing gas
questions.question: Which gas is commonly called "laughing gas"?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Nitrous oxide (N₂O)
Why: Nitrous oxide, N₂O, causes a mild feeling of happiness when inhaled and is used as a mild anaesthetic in dentistry.
Why not the others: (A) is a brown, poisonous gas from vehicle exhausts. (B) is a colourless gas formed in lightning and engines. (C) is a pungent gas used to make fertilisers.
Key point: N₂O is also a greenhouse gas.

questions.sub_topic: Assumption behind a notice to use the stairs
questions.question:
Statement: A notice in an office says, "Use the stairs instead of the lift and stay healthy."
Assumptions:
I. Climbing stairs is good exercise.
II. The lift in the office is out of order.
Which of the assumptions is implicit?
options: C) Both I and II are implicit
D) Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Only I is implicit
Answer steps: The notice links using the stairs with staying healthy, so it takes for granted that climbing stairs is good exercise (I). It does not say the lift is broken; it asks people to choose the stairs, so II is not assumed.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) accept II, which would make the advice about health pointless. (D) rejects I, on which the notice depends.
Key point: An assumption is what the speaker must believe for the statement to make sense.

questions.sub_topic: Length of a row after two people swap
questions.question: In a row, A is 10th from the left end and B is 15th from the right end. When A and B interchange their positions, A becomes 18th from the left end. How many people are in the row?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 32
Answer steps: after the swap A stands in B's old place, so B's old place is 18th from the left. It is also 15th from the right. Total = 18 + 15 − 1 = 32.
Why not the others: (A) forgets to subtract 1. (B) uses A's old position (10 + 15 + 3). (C) adds all the numbers given.
Key point: Total = position from left + position from right − 1, for the same place.

questions.sub_topic: Body replaced by NITI Aayog
questions.question: NITI Aayog, set up on 1 January 2015, replaced which body?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Planning Commission
Why: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission, which had been set up in 1950. The Prime Minister is its chairperson.
Why not the others: (B) is a constitutional body (Article 280) that still exists. (C) and (D) were not replaced by NITI Aayog.
Key point: Planning Commission 1950 → NITI Aayog 2015.

questions.sub_topic: Letter series with growing gaps
questions.question: Which letter should come next in B, E, I, N, … ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) T
Answer steps: B (2), E (5), I (9), N (14) — the gaps are +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6: 14 + 6 = 20, which is T.
Why not the others: (A) S (19) adds only +5 again. (B) U (21) adds +7. (C) R (18) adds +4.
Key point: Convert letters to their positions and look at the differences.

questions.sub_topic: Dams and the rivers they are built on
questions.question:
Match the dams in List-I with the rivers on which they are built in List-II:

List-I
(A) Bhakra Nangal Dam
(B) Hirakud Dam
(C) Sardar Sarovar Dam
(D) Tehri Dam

List-II
(I) Narmada
(II) Bhagirathi
(III) Sutlej
(IV) Mahanadi
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Bhakra Nangal — Sutlej, Himachal Pradesh–Punjab (III); Hirakud — Mahanadi, Odisha (IV); Sardar Sarovar — Narmada, Gujarat (I); Tehri — Bhagirathi, Uttarakhand (II).
Why not the others: (B) swaps Bhakra and Hirakud; (C) swaps Sardar Sarovar and Tehri; (D) swaps Hirakud and Sardar Sarovar.
Key point: Hirakud is one of the longest earthen dams in the world.

questions.sub_topic: Angle between clock hands at 3:40
questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 130°
Answer steps: angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30 × 3 − 5.5 × 40| = |90 − 220| = 130°.
Why not the others: (A) forgets that the hour hand has moved 20° past the 3 in 40 minutes (240° − 90° = 150°). (C) counts only the four hour-gaps from 4 to 8 (4 × 30°). (D) is the reflex angle, 360° − 130°.
Key point: The hour hand moves 0.5° every minute; the minute hand moves 6°.

questions.sub_topic: Syllogism with no book a bag
questions.question:
Statements:
Some pens are books.
No book is a bag.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are not bags.
II. No pen is a bag.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Only I follows
Answer steps: The pens that are books cannot be bags, because no book is a bag, so "Some pens are not bags" is certain. The other pens (those that are not books) may or may not be bags, so "No pen is a bag" is not certain.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) accept II, which goes beyond the pens that are books. (D) rejects I, which is certain.
Key point: "Some A are B" + "No B is C" gives "Some A are not C".

questions.sub_topic: Statements about Census 2027
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about India's Census 2027:
A. It is the first census in India to collect data digitally, through mobile applications.
B. It includes the enumeration of caste.
C. For most of the country, the reference date is 00:00 hours on 1 March 2027.
D. The whole census is carried out in a single phase in 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A, B and C only
Why: A is correct: Census 2027 is India's first digital census, with an option for households to enumerate themselves online. B is correct: the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs decided on 30 April 2025 to include caste enumeration. C is correct: the reference date is 1 March 2027, except for snow-bound areas such as Ladakh and parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand (1 October 2026).
Why not the others: D is wrong: the census has two phases — houselisting and housing census (1 April to 30 September 2026) and population enumeration (February 2027). Options (C) and (D) include D; (B) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: Census 2027 is India's 16th census and the first since 2011.

questions.sub_topic: Students who play only football
questions.question: In a group of 80 students, every student plays cricket or football or both. If 50 play cricket and 40 play football, how many play only football?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 30
Answer steps: both = 50 + 40 − 80 = 10. Only football = 40 − 10 = 30.
Why not the others: (A) counts everyone who plays football, including those who also play cricket. (B) is the number who play both. (D) subtracts the "both" group twice.
Key point: "Only B" = n(B) − n(both).

questions.sub_topic: Article that abolishes untouchability
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Article 17
Why: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; enforcing any disability arising from it is an offence punishable by law (Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955).
Why not the others: (A) forbids discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. (C) protects six freedoms, such as speech and movement. (D) forbids trafficking in human beings and forced labour.
Key point: Articles 14–18 form the Right to Equality.

questions.sub_topic: Sum of cubes from sum and product
questions.question: If a + b = 5 and ab = 6, what is the value of a³ + b³?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 35
Given: a + b = 5, ab = 6.
Step 1: a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b).
Step 2: = 125 − 3 × 6 × 5 = 125 − 90 = 35. (Check: a = 2, b = 3 gives 8 + 27 = 35.)
Common mistake: stopping at (a + b)³ = 125 (option A), or adding 90 instead of subtracting it (215, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Expression with swapped operation signs
questions.question: If '+' means '×', '−' means '÷', '×' means '−' and '÷' means '+', what is the value of 16 − 4 + 3 × 5 ÷ 2?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 9
Answer steps: replace the signs: 16 ÷ 4 × 3 − 5 + 2. Then 16 ÷ 4 = 4; 4 × 3 = 12; 12 − 5 + 2 = 9.
Why not the others: (A) works 12 − (5 + 2), breaking the left-to-right order. (B) reads '×' as '+' and '÷' as '−' (12 + 5 − 2). (C) reads both '×' and '÷' as '+' (12 + 5 + 2).
Key point: Replace every sign first, then follow BODMAS.

questions.sub_topic: Layers of the atmosphere in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following layers of the atmosphere in order, starting from the Earth's surface:
A. Mesosphere
B. Troposphere
C. Thermosphere
D. Stratosphere
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) B, D, A, C
Why: Troposphere (where weather occurs, up to about 8–18 km), stratosphere (with the ozone layer), mesosphere (where meteors burn up) and thermosphere (where the ionosphere and auroras are found).
Why not the others: (A) puts the mesosphere below the stratosphere. (B) starts with the stratosphere. (C) puts the thermosphere below the mesosphere.
Key point: Troposphere → stratosphere → mesosphere → thermosphere → exosphere.

questions.sub_topic: Scheduling five lectures across a week
questions.question: Five lectures P, Q, R, S and T are held from Monday to Friday, one each day. Q is on Wednesday. R is held on the day immediately after P. T is not held on Monday or Friday. S is held on a day before Q. Which lecture is held on Friday?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) R
Answer steps: P and R must be on two days in a row other than Wednesday: Monday–Tuesday or Thursday–Friday. If they were Monday–Tuesday, S could not be before Wednesday. So P is on Thursday and R on Friday. T cannot be on Monday, so T is on Tuesday and S on Monday.
Why not the others: (A) P is on Thursday. (B) T is on Tuesday. (C) S is on Monday.
Key point: Test the few possible places for a linked pair and reject the one that breaks a rule.

questions.sub_topic: Why sound cannot cross a vacuum
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
Reason (R): Sound is a mechanical wave, which needs a material medium to travel.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. Sound travels as compressions and rarefactions of the particles of a medium (solid, liquid or gas). In a vacuum there are no particles to vibrate, so sound cannot pass — which is why (R) explains (A). (Light, an electromagnetic wave, can cross a vacuum.)
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Astronauts on a spacewalk talk by radio, not by sound through space.

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on multiples of six
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Every number that is divisible by 6 is also divisible by 3.
Reason (R): 6 = 2 × 3, so every multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: (A) is true (12, 18, 24 … are all divisible by 3). (R) is true and gives the reason: a multiple of 6 is 6k = 3 × 2k, which is a multiple of 3.
Why not the others: (B) denies a link that (R) states directly. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: If 3 is a factor of 6, it is a factor of every multiple of 6.

questions.sub_topic: Glands and the hormones they secrete
questions.question:
Match the glands in List-I with the hormones they secrete in List-II:

List-I
(A) Pancreas
(B) Thyroid
(C) Adrenal gland
(D) Pituitary gland

List-II
(I) Adrenaline
(II) Growth hormone
(III) Insulin
(IV) Thyroxine
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Pancreas — insulin, which lowers blood sugar (III); thyroid — thyroxine, which controls metabolism (IV); adrenal — adrenaline, the "fight or flight" hormone (I); pituitary — growth hormone (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the pancreas and thyroid; (B) swaps the adrenal and pituitary; (D) swaps the thyroid and adrenal.
Key point: Lack of insulin causes diabetes; lack of iodine for thyroxine causes goitre.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the Western Ghats
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Western Ghats:
A. They are one of the world's biodiversity hotspots.
B. They were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.
C. They run parallel to the eastern coast of India.
D. Silent Valley National Park lies in the Western Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A, B and D only
Why: A is correct: the Western Ghats (with Sri Lanka) form one of the global biodiversity hotspots, rich in endemic plants and animals. B is correct (inscribed in 2012). D is correct: Silent Valley, in Kerala's Palakkad district, is in the Nilgiri hills of the Western Ghats.
Why not the others: C is wrong: the Western Ghats run along the western coast; the Eastern Ghats lie near the east coast. Options (C) and (D) include C; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: India has parts of four hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka and Sundaland.

questions.sub_topic: Share of a partner who joins later
questions.question: A and B start a business with ₹40,000 and ₹60,000. After 6 months, C joins with ₹80,000. Out of a profit of ₹63,000 at the end of the year, what is C's share?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) ₹18,000
Given: A ₹40,000 for 12 months; B ₹60,000 for 12 months; C ₹80,000 for 6 months.
Step 1: Capital × time — A 480, B 720, C 480 (in thousand-rupee months), so the ratio is 2 : 3 : 2.
Step 2: C's share = 2/7 × 63,000 = ₹18,000.
Common mistake: ignoring the time C invested (ratio 2 : 3 : 4, giving C ₹28,000, option A), or splitting the profit equally (₹21,000, option D).

questions.sub_topic: HCF of three numbers
questions.question: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 72, 108 and 180?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 36
Given: 72 = 2³ × 3²; 108 = 2² × 3³; 180 = 2² × 3² × 5.
Step 1: Take the lowest power of each common prime: 2² and 3².
Step 2: HCF = 4 × 9 = 36.
Common mistake: taking the highest powers instead, which gives the LCM (2³ × 3³ × 5 = 1080, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Straits and the land masses they separate
questions.question:
Match the straits in List-I with the land masses they separate in List-II:

List-I
(A) Palk Strait
(B) Strait of Gibraltar
(C) Bering Strait
(D) Strait of Malacca

List-II
(I) Asia (Russia) and North America (Alaska)
(II) Malay Peninsula and the island of Sumatra
(III) India and Sri Lanka
(IV) Europe (Spain) and Africa (Morocco)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Palk Strait — India and Sri Lanka (III); Strait of Gibraltar — Spain and Morocco, joining the Atlantic to the Mediterranean (IV); Bering Strait — Russia and Alaska (I); Strait of Malacca — Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, one of the busiest shipping lanes (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Palk and Gibraltar; (B) swaps Bering and Malacca; (C) swaps Gibraltar and Bering.
Key point: A strait is a narrow waterway joining two larger bodies of water.

questions.sub_topic: Probability that two dice total eight
questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 8?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 5/36
Given: 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes.
Step 1: Pairs with sum 8: (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2) — 5 outcomes.
Step 2: Probability = 5/36.
Common mistake: counting (2, 6) and (6, 2) as one outcome, or using the count for a sum of 7, which has 6 outcomes (1/6, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Partner agency of ISRO in the NISAR mission
questions.question: NISAR, an Earth-observation satellite launched on 30 July 2025 aboard GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota, is a joint mission of ISRO and which agency?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) NASA (USA)
Why: NISAR stands for NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar. NASA supplied the L-band radar and ISRO the S-band radar, the satellite bus and the launch. It maps the Earth's land and ice surfaces about every 12 days.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are space agencies that are not partners in NISAR (CNES works with ISRO on other missions such as TRISHNA).
Key point: It was the first GSLV launch into a Sun-synchronous orbit.

questions.sub_topic: Difference between compound and simple interest
questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum, interest compounded annually?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ₹20
Given: P = ₹8,000, R = 5%, T = 2 years.
Step 1: Simple interest = 8000 × 5 × 2 ÷ 100 = ₹800.
Step 2: Compound interest = 8000 × (1.05)² − 8000 = 8820 − 8000 = ₹820.
Step 3: Difference = 820 − 800 = ₹20. (Shortcut for 2 years: P × (R/100)² = 8000 × 1/400 = ₹20.)
Common mistake: giving the simple interest itself (₹800, option C), or doubling the shortcut (₹40, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Home state of Kathakali
questions.question: Kathakali, a classical dance known for its elaborate make-up and costumes, comes from which state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Kerala
Why: Kathakali is a dance-drama of Kerala that tells stories from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, with painted faces (green for heroic characters).
Why not the others: (A) is the home of Bharatanatyam. (B) of Kuchipudi. (C) of Manipuri.
Key point: Kerala is also the home of Mohiniyattam.

questions.sub_topic: Language of Heart Lamp, International Booker 2025 winner
questions.question: "Heart Lamp", the story collection by Banu Mushtaq that won the International Booker Prize 2025, was translated into English by Deepa Bhasthi from which language?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Kannada
Why: Heart Lamp, a collection of 12 Kannada stories, won the prize on 20 May 2025. It was the first book translated from Kannada and the first short-story collection to win; Deepa Bhasthi became the first Indian translator to win it.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are other South Indian languages; no book translated from them has won the prize.
Key point: Geetanjali Shree's "Tomb of Sand" (Hindi) won in 2022.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the President of India
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the President of India:
A. The President is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies.
B. A candidate must be at least 35 years old.
C. The President can be removed by impeachment under Article 61.
D. The President holds office for a term of six years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B, C and D
C) A, B and C only
D) B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A, B and C only
Why: A is correct (Article 54; the elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry assemblies also vote). B is correct (Article 58). C is correct: impeachment for violation of the Constitution is under Article 61.
Why not the others: D is wrong: the term is five years (Article 56). Options (B) and (D) include D; (A) leaves out the correct statement C.
Key point: Nominated members of Parliament do not vote in the presidential election.

questions.sub_topic: Opponent in India's first Women's World Cup final win
questions.question: India won its first ICC Women's Cricket World Cup on 2 November 2025 at Navi Mumbai by defeating which team in the final?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) South Africa
Why: India, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, scored 298/7 and bowled South Africa out for 246 to win by 52 runs at the DY Patil Stadium. Shafali Verma was Player of the Match and Deepti Sharma Player of the Tournament.
Why not the others: India beat Australia in the semi-final. England and New Zealand did not reach the final.
Key point: It was India's first title in the Women's ODI World Cup, after losing the finals of 2005 and 2017.

questions.sub_topic: Present age from two age ratios
questions.question: The present ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 7 : 2. After 10 years, the ratio will be 9 : 4. What is the father's present age?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 35 years
Given: present ages 7x and 2x.
Step 1: After 10 years: (7x + 10) : (2x + 10) = 9 : 4.
Step 2: 4(7x + 10) = 9(2x + 10), so 28x + 40 = 18x + 90, and 10x = 50, x = 5.
Step 3: Father = 7 × 5 = 35 years (son 10 years; after 10 years, 45 : 20 = 9 : 4).
Common mistake: giving the father's age after 10 years (45 years, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Selling price for a new profit after a loss
questions.question: By selling a watch for ₹540, a man loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 15%?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹690
Given: selling price ₹540 at a loss of 10%.
Step 1: Cost price = 540 ÷ 0.90 = ₹600.
Step 2: For a gain of 15%, selling price = 600 × 1.15 = ₹690.
Common mistake: applying 15% to the old selling price (540 × 1.15 = ₹621, option A); the profit percentage is always on the cost price.

questions.sub_topic: Coding a word by the sum of letter positions
questions.question: In a certain code, PEN is written as 35, because P = 16, E = 5 and N = 14. How is INK written in that code?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 34
Answer steps: I = 9, N = 14, K = 11, so INK = 9 + 14 + 11 = 34.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) come from taking K as 10 or 13. (C) is the code for PEN, not INK.
Key point: Check the rule on the given word before applying it.

questions.sub_topic: Blood group called the universal donor
questions.question: People with which blood group are called universal donors?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) O
Why: Group O red cells carry neither the A nor the B antigen, so they are not attacked by the antibodies in the blood of other groups. (Strictly, O negative is the universal donor for red cells.)
Why not the others: (B) AB is the universal recipient, since its plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B. (C) and (D) can give only to their own group and to AB.
Key point: O — universal donor; AB — universal recipient.

questions.sub_topic: Conditions needed for rusting
questions.question: Which of the following must both be present for iron to rust?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Oxygen and water (moisture)
Why: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide. It forms only when iron is in contact with both oxygen (air) and water. Iron nails kept in dry air or in boiled water sealed with oil do not rust.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) leave out oxygen or water, or add gases that are not needed.
Key point: Painting, oiling and galvanising (a zinc coat) prevent rusting by keeping air and water away.

questions.sub_topic: Round trip of a boat on a river
questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How long will the boat take to go 36 km downstream and come back to the starting point?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 5 hours
Given: still-water speed 15 km/h; stream 3 km/h; distance 36 km each way.
Step 1: Downstream speed = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h, time = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 hours.
Step 2: Upstream speed = 15 − 3 = 12 km/h, time = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 hours.
Step 3: Total = 5 hours.
Common mistake: ignoring the stream (72 ÷ 15 = 4.8 hours, option A), or using the downstream speed both ways (72 ÷ 18 = 4 hours, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Mirror used as a rear-view mirror
questions.question: Drivers use a mirror that gives an upright, smaller image and a wide view of the road behind. What kind of mirror is it?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Convex mirror
Why: A convex mirror always forms an erect, smaller image and gives a wider field of view, so the driver can see more of the traffic behind.
Why not the others: (A) is used in torches, shaving mirrors and by dentists. (B) gives a narrow view. (D) is not used for this purpose.
Key point: Convex — wide view; concave — magnified view or a parallel beam.

questions.sub_topic: Tank filled by two pipes with an outlet open
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 12 hours
Given: A fills 1/10, B fills 1/15 and C empties 1/12 of the tank per hour.
Step 1: Net rate = 1/10 + 1/15 − 1/12 = 6/60 + 4/60 − 5/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.
Step 2: Time = 12 hours.
Common mistake: adding C as if it also filled the tank (15/60 = 1/4, so 4 hours, option B), or ignoring C (A and B alone take 6 hours, option C).

questions.sub_topic: City with the highest four-month rainfall
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Monthly rainfall (in mm) recorded in four cities during the monsoon

| City | June | July | August | September |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashpur | 120 | 280 | 240 | 160 |
| Bhimgarh | 90 | 210 | 180 | 120 |
| Chandnagar | 150 | 330 | 300 | 120 |
| Devipur | 60 | 150 | 140 | 50 |

Question: Which city received the highest total rainfall over the four months?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Chandnagar
Given: four-month totals — Ashpur 120 + 280 + 240 + 160 = 800; Bhimgarh 90 + 210 + 180 + 120 = 600; Chandnagar 150 + 330 + 300 + 120 = 900; Devipur 60 + 150 + 140 + 50 = 400.
Step 1: Compare the totals: 900 > 800 > 600 > 400.
Step 2: The highest is Chandnagar (900 mm).
Common mistake: looking at one month only — Ashpur has more rain than Chandnagar in September, but less over the whole season.

questions.sub_topic: Average monthly rainfall of Ashpur
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Monthly rainfall (in mm) recorded in four cities during the monsoon

| City | June | July | August | September |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashpur | 120 | 280 | 240 | 160 |
| Bhimgarh | 90 | 210 | 180 | 120 |
| Chandnagar | 150 | 330 | 300 | 120 |
| Devipur | 60 | 150 | 140 | 50 |

Question: What was the average monthly rainfall of Ashpur over the four months?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 200 mm
Given: Ashpur — 120, 280, 240 and 160 mm.
Step 1: Total = 120 + 280 + 240 + 160 = 800 mm.
Step 2: Average = 800 ÷ 4 = 200 mm.
Common mistake: dividing the total by 5 instead of 4 (160 mm, option C), or giving the August figure (240 mm, option B).

questions.sub_topic: July share of Bhimgarh's rainfall
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Monthly rainfall (in mm) recorded in four cities during the monsoon

| City | June | July | August | September |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashpur | 120 | 280 | 240 | 160 |
| Bhimgarh | 90 | 210 | 180 | 120 |
| Chandnagar | 150 | 330 | 300 | 120 |
| Devipur | 60 | 150 | 140 | 50 |

Question: What percentage of Bhimgarh's four-month rainfall fell in July?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 35%
Given: Bhimgarh July = 210 mm; Bhimgarh total = 90 + 210 + 180 + 120 = 600 mm.
Step 1: 210 ÷ 600 = 0.35.
Step 2: As a percentage, 35%.
Common mistake: dividing by 1000 instead of the city's own total (21%, option D), or using August (180 ÷ 600 = 30%, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Ratio of August rainfall in two cities
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Monthly rainfall (in mm) recorded in four cities during the monsoon

| City | June | July | August | September |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashpur | 120 | 280 | 240 | 160 |
| Bhimgarh | 90 | 210 | 180 | 120 |
| Chandnagar | 150 | 330 | 300 | 120 |
| Devipur | 60 | 150 | 140 | 50 |

Question: What is the ratio of the August rainfall of Chandnagar to that of Bhimgarh?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 5 : 3
Given: August — Chandnagar 300 mm, Bhimgarh 180 mm.
Step 1: 300 : 180.
Step 2: Divide both by 60: 5 : 3.
Common mistake: writing the ratio the wrong way round (3 : 5, option A), or using July for Bhimgarh (300 : 210 = 10 : 7, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Cities where September rain was below half of July
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Monthly rainfall (in mm) recorded in four cities during the monsoon

| City | June | July | August | September |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashpur | 120 | 280 | 240 | 160 |
| Bhimgarh | 90 | 210 | 180 | 120 |
| Chandnagar | 150 | 330 | 300 | 120 |
| Devipur | 60 | 150 | 140 | 50 |

Question: In how many of the four cities was the September rainfall less than half of the July rainfall?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 2
Given: half of July — Ashpur 140, Bhimgarh 105, Chandnagar 165, Devipur 75; September — 160, 120, 120, 50.
Step 1: Ashpur 160 > 140 (no); Bhimgarh 120 > 105 (no).
Step 2: Chandnagar 120 < 165 (yes); Devipur 50 < 75 (yes).
Step 3: Two cities qualify.
Common mistake: comparing September with June instead of July, or counting Ashpur and Bhimgarh because their rainfall also fell from July to September.
